evals.name: critique-wp-event-metabox
evals.prompt: Please review the meta box in evals/fixtures/wp-event-metabox/event-fields.php. Editors (two part-time staff, desktop) use it to enter a new event and publish it. Tell me what is wrong from the editors' point of view and what to fix first.
evals.expected_output: A structured critique per dimension with evidence levels, severities, blockers marked, and specific small recommendations. States that it could not render the interface.
assertions: The report finds that placeholders are used instead of labels
The report finds that required fields are not marked and that saving silently skips them without any message
The report finds that the 20+ fields are not grouped
The report finds that the price error is shown only by color
Each finding carries an evidence level (Observed, Hypothesis or Assumption)
The report states that the UI was not rendered and treats perception findings as Hypotheses
The report does not claim measured contrast ratios or target sizes
The report does not call the nonce or capability check in the save handler missing
No overall single score hides blocker dimensions

evals.name: design-wp-event-fields
evals.prompt: I build WordPress sites. For an 'Event' post type my editors need to enter title, start and end date, location with address and map link, indoor or outdoor, capacity, price, a featured flag, an image, up to five links, contact data, internal notes and SEO fields. Two part-time editors, desktop. Plan how this interface should be structured for them. Do not write code.
evals.expected_output: A design brief: tasks, field inventory, grouping and order, wireframe, labels and help text in editor language, conditional display and defaults, states and error messages, host constraints, open questions.
assertions: Fields are grouped by editor task (for example when and where, price, media, contact, extras) and ordered by work sequence
Rarely used fields (internal notes, SEO) are placed behind progressive disclosure
Labels are written in editor language and help text is provided where needed
Required fields are marked and validation messages say what is wrong and how to fix it
The brief uses the host's own components and does not propose overriding core styles
WordPress-specific statements are marked as Assumptions or not verified against current documentation
The report contains no code and changes no files
Open questions or assumptions about the editors are stated, not invented
